text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour tells parliamentary committee government plans to study carefully issue of retirement in the civil service and address the merging of ministries.
- King Hussein heads the graduation of women military cadet recruits and witnesses a display by Indonesian special unit commandoes.
- U.S. helps Jordan in projects to improve water quality.
- U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross expected in Amman; Jordanian Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarwanah says Jordan will stress an initiative which finds acceptance with the Palestinians.
- Two youths and a girl behind the slaying of a young man along the road to Rishadiyah, in the south.
- Jordan to send relief aid to the victims of the quake in Iran; Crown Prince Hassan sends condolences to Iranian people.
- Supply ministry officials says no crisis in meat supplies.

- Jordan's southern regions expected to benefit from the transfer of the Red Sea port of Aqaba to a free trade zone; tourism and services projects set up in the region will be exempt from income tax on up to 75 percent of profits.
- Jordan tries to revive a proposed $300 million regasification plant in Aqaba using Qatari gas brought by vessels.
- Leading Islamist deputy calls for setting up a committee to deal with drought in the southern areas of the kingdom.
- Ensour denies plans to lay off public employees.
- Cabinet enacts long awaited companies and securities laws, reforms expected to lure foreign investments; shares climb 0.71 percent.
- Crown Prince calls for linking vocational academic education to serve labour market.
